steps.body: Two-step stories often need a trade. 52 stickers, give away 27 (that's 25), then get 13 back: 25 + 13 = 38.
steps.narration: Two-step stories often need a trade. Fifty-two stickers, give away twenty-seven, then get thirteen back: fifty-two minus twenty-seven needs a break, twenty-five, then twenty-five plus thirteen is thirty-eight.

steps.body: Do the first step (it breaks a ten).

widget.prompt: Work out 52 − 27. Tap the ones column and break one ten when 2 ones are not enough.

commonResults.feedback: 35 flips 2 − 7 into 7 − 2. Break one of the 5 tens, then subtract in place.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Break 52 into 4 tens and 12 ones. Then 12 − 7 = 5 and 4 − 2 = 2, so 25.
widget.successFeedback: You broke one ten: 4 tens 12 ones. Then 52 − 27 = 25.

predict.prompt: In 52 − 27, what must happen before you can take 7 ones from 2 ones?
predict.reveal: The column model breaks one ten into 10 ones, so 52 becomes 4 tens and 12 ones. Now 12 − 7 can be shown.

explanationVariants: Give away first (with a break), then get some back: 38 stickers.

widget.prompt: A collector has 52 stickers. They give away 27, then get 13 back. How many stickers do they have now?

commonErrors.feedback: That's only step one — 13 come back: 25 + 13 = 38.
That subtracted the 13 too. You GET them back, so add: 25 + 13 = 38.

steps.body: A story can also **add** into a trade. 46 + 17: ones 6 + 7 make 13, so trade a ten → 63.
steps.narration: A story can also add into a trade. Forty-six plus seventeen: the ones six plus seven make thirteen, so trade a ten, sixty-three. Then keep going.

steps.body: Match each first-step to its result.

widget.prompt: Each first step trades. Match it to its total.
widget.missFeedback: Trade when ones reach ten; break when the top ones fall short.
widget.successFeedback: Every trade handled — first steps done!

explanationVariants: Add into the trade (63), then take 23 away: 40.

widget.prompt: Maya has 46 shells. She finds 17 more, then gives away 23. How many shells does she have now?

commonErrors.feedback: That's only step one — 23 given away: 63 − 23 = 40.
That did 46 − 17 + 23. The 17 are FOUND (add), the 23 given (subtract): 63 − 23 = 40.

explanationVariants: 60 − 35: the ones are 0 and 5 — 0 can't lose 5, so break a ten. 60 − 35 = 25.
Zero ones on top means a break is needed: 25.

options.label: nothing — just subtract
options.feedback: The top ones are 0, which can't lose 5. Break a ten: 60 − 35 = 25.

options.label: break a ten — 0 can't lose 5
options.feedback: Yes — 60 is 5 tens 10 ones after the break; 10 − 5 = 5, 5 − 3 = 2 → 25.

options.label: trade a ten up
options.feedback: Trading up is for adding. Subtracting with too-few ones needs a BREAK: 25.

explanationVariants: Break for the subtract (25), then add 18 back: 43.

widget.prompt: A bakery has 60 cookies. It sells 35, then bakes 18 more. How many cookies does it have now?

commonErrors.feedback: That's only step one — 18 more are baked: 25 + 18 = 43.
That subtracted the 18 too. Baking ADDS: 25 + 18 = 43.

takeaways: A step may trade (adding) or break (subtracting).
Do each step fully before the next.
Watch whether each event adds or removes.
steps.teaser: next: picking the right two steps yourself.

concept.body: Slow down. 41 − 15, then + 6. Step 1 breaks a ten: 41 − 15 = 26. Step 2: 26 + 6 = 32.
concept.narration: Slow it down. Forty-one minus fifteen, then plus six. Step one breaks a ten: forty-one minus fifteen is twenty-six. Step two: twenty-six plus six is thirty-two.

explanationVariants: Break for the subtract, then add 6: 32.

commonErrors.feedback: That's only step one — add the 6: 26 + 6 = 32.
That subtracted the 6 too. Step two ADDS: 26 + 6 = 32.
